summary: This document outlines an assignment to build, train, and evaluate a custom tiny language model using nanoGPT and PyTorch. Students must perform two experiments: one with a starter corpus and another with an expanded corpus, and then interact with the model via a chat interface.
key_facts: Use Andrej Karpathy's nanoGPT model with PyTorch.
The model uses a small word-token transformer with 64-number embeddings and a 48-token context window.
Students must perform two experiments: a starter-corpus experiment and a corpus-extension experiment.
Submit a public GitHub repository containing the executed notebook, results, and a working chat interface.
The assignment is graded out of 10 based on deliverable quality, testing & evaluation, and working result.
The 48-case synthetic language eval suite must be run before and after training for both experiments.
The chat interface can be a terminal or notebook loop, but must produce actual replies from the trained model.
Use only corpus material you have permission to use and share.

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.definition: A neural network architecture used for language modeling.
concepts.in_this_source: The assignment uses a nanoGPT model which is a word-token transformer.

concepts.name: PyTorch
concepts.in_this_source: The assignment uses PyTorch for training the model and running the notebook.

concepts.name: Eval Leakage
concepts.definition: Test prompts or answers leaking into training data, which inflates evaluation scores without real learning.
concepts.in_this_source: The brief threatens a substantial grade penalty if eval prompts, answer keys, or eval outputs are included in the training corpus.

concepts.name: Corpus
concepts.definition: A collection of texts used for training a language model.
concepts.in_this_source: The assignment requires students to choose a corpus and expand it for a second experiment.

concepts.name: Hyperparameters
concepts.definition: Settings used to control the learning process in a neural network.
concepts.in_this_source: The assignment requires students to choose training steps and a learning rate as hyperparameters.
